hero.title2: grown for one, built for anyone
hero.sub: A personal embodied AI — a constitution for a personality, curated memory for a life, and a self-developed core that answers to you alone. Not a platform. Not an assistant farm. One companion, grown for one person, engineered so anyone can run it.
hero.badgeLocal: Runs on your machine · loopback by default
start.title: Get Started
start.sub: Three steps from a clone to a running local console: fetch the repository, run the one-command installer, then fill the slots in the guided wizard.
start.step1Body: I'm AiDog ships from a private repository — clone access required.
start.step2Body: One command: provision + boot + verify. The installer is idempotent, so re-running it is always safe.
start.step3Body: The guided wizard prompts for every credential — hidden input on a terminal, values never echoed; output names slots and lengths only. The console's Overview ACTIVATION card mirrors the same check, each row with a FIX deep-link.
start.roadmap: Public download & hosted docs land with the public release.
skills.title: Skills
skills.sub: A small, curated capability layer. Skills are screened deterministically before they ever reach the model, and only trusted, reviewed entries are recommended — no open marketplace, no supply-chain surprises.
skills.emptyBody: No recommended skills are listed yet. We would rather show an honest empty shelf than fill it with names we cannot vouch for. Recommendations land here one by one as they pass review.
skills.emptyCta: Propose a skill on GitHub Issues
skills.step1Body: Publish your skill repository on GitHub and open an issue with the link and a short description of what it does.
skills.step2Body: We read the code: permissions, network behaviour, data handling. Skills must pass the deterministic router checks and our security review.
skills.step3Body: Approved skills appear in the recommended shelf above and mount into your local install — read-only sources, revocable at any time.
caps.title: Capabilities
caps.sub: What the product actually does, card by card — every line comes from the release gates and the capability docs, nothing invented. The full docs open with the public release.
caps.c1B: Console chat streams by SSE and Telegram replies stream behind a typing heartbeat, so an answer reaches you as it is written.
caps.c2B: Local speech-to-text sessions with fuzzy wake phrases, TTS announcements through your own engine key, BYOK image generation and Telegram photo send.
caps.c3B: Skills ship as SKILL.md with industry-standard frontmatter; the deterministic router picks the TOP3 candidates before any body loads — 30/30.
caps.c4B: Curated long-term memory in bounded Markdown budgets with archive tiers, plus a user-profile layer — memory suite 58/58, no vector store you cannot read.
caps.c5B: Schedule in plain language — /cron ship the report tomorrow 9am parses into a job that stays fail-closed until you enable it — while /learn and /reflect grow the loop behind lint-gated writes.
caps.c6B: Telegram is live; nine adapters — Discord / Slack / Email / Webhook / DingTalk / Feishu / WeChat / WhatsApp / Signal — each reports an honest status and stays silent while unconfigured.
caps.c7B: An Electron frameless shell with transparency slider, always-on-top and tray — Linux packaging verified, Win/macOS honestly not built yet; desktop suite 15/15.
caps.c8B: AIDOG_PROFILE selects fully isolated profiles — settings, secrets, state and body kept apart — proven by a 63/63 isolation gate and an 18-leg real-machine E2E.
caps.c9B: The shell backend is grammar-checked local, Docker or SSH; execute_code folds into at most 8 steps with checkpointed file writes you can restore.
caps.c10B: Up to three isolated parallel delegates with fresh context, plus an MCP client for stdio and HTTP servers with tool allow/deny filtering.
caps.c11B: Six lifecycle events can run your own command on a timeout — the child gets only PATH and HOME, never a credential — and context dirs pull shared files into a turn.
caps.c12B: The loopback console exposes GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions — streaming and non-streaming — behind a Bearer token for OpenAI-style tooling.
caps.web3Title: Web3 — orders only through a human gate
caps.web3Sub: Nine venues in one catalog: keyless chain reads (Jupiter, Velora, Hyperliquid, dYdX, GMX, public RPC) beside slot-gated CEX accounts (OKX, Kraken, Binance), all behind six exchange_* tools. Public market data needs no credential; with no slot configured, the order tool never registers at all.
caps.w3p1B: exchange_prepare_order is a dry run: it stores a plan — venue, side, symbol, quantity, price — and touches nothing.
caps.w3p2B: You review the plan in the console and approve or reject it behind the local Bearer token. Thresholds ship at 0, so every plan waits for a human.
caps.w3p3B: exchange_execute_order takes a plan id and nothing else — every field is read back from the stored plan, then re-checked fail-closed against the day's ledger. Market orders never auto-approve at any threshold.
caps.web3Note: Withdrawals, on-chain transfers and transaction signing do not exist in the core at all — no function, no endpoint, no settings key can move funds off a venue. The core suite asserts that absence against the source.
console.title: Console
console.sub: Local Web Console Preview — see the panel you get after installing, before you download anything.
console.tag: STATIC PREVIEW — live values render locally on your machine after install
console.ovSub: Services, usage and channel at a glance
console.voiceLockSub: tap the orb to unlock voice
console.reactorNote: usage tallies locally — nothing is uploaded
console.f1B: Status, settings, usage, events and voice — a situational console, not an admin warehouse.
console.f2B: Serves on 127.0.0.1 with plain standard library code; write operations require your local access token.
console.f3B: Chat where you already are, inspect where it runs. Both faces speak English and Chinese.
console.f4B: The first Overview card mirrors the wizard's check — required slots, endpoint reachability, service state — and every failing row carries a FIX deep-link.
console.f5B: 32 runtime slots are editable from Settings; values are write-only and never echoed — output names slots and lengths.
console.f6B: Run doctor, restart the chat service and apply an update from the panel; an upgrade banner appears the moment a newer release exists.
models.title: Models & Transparency
models.sub: We will publish how this product actually runs — which models serve it and how much compute it consumes. No estimates, no marketing charts: only what the software itself reports.
models.status: COMING ONLINE — statistics service not yet live
models.statusBody: The aggregation service is being built. Until it ships, this page shows the pipeline design — and nothing else. Any number here before launch would be a lie, so there are none.
models.chartNote: Data will appear here once the stats API goes live
models.p1B: The local app optionally reports just two things: the model name in use and cumulative token counts — anonymously, and only if you opt in.
models.p2B: A free-tier edge worker receives the reports and writes them into a free-tier edge database. Free-tier only, consistent with the free constitution.
models.p3B: The chart above reads a public JSON endpoint from that database and renders aggregate model usage — published totals only, never per-user records.
security.title: Security & Trust
security.sub: Local-first by construction — the quiet guarantees, stated plainly.
security.s1B: Services listen on 127.0.0.1 only — reachable from your machine, not from your network.
security.s2B: Secrets live in one gitignored file (mode 0600). Output and logs report slot names and lengths — never values.
security.s3B: Every console write operation requires your local access token.
security.s4B: Usage tallies on your machine. Nothing leaves it unless you opt in.
security.s5B: The interface speaks English and Chinese; all source code is written in English.
security.s6B: Permanently free — no paid tier, no in-app purchase, no usage fee, ever.
arch.title: Architecture
arch.sub: Three layers, strictly separated — so the core underneath can be swapped without losing who you are.
arch.kB: Replaceable — a transitional kernel runs today while the self-developed core is under construction.
arch.bB: Constitution · curated memory · skills · stance · persona — owned by this repo, independent of any kernel.
arch.cB: Chain access and project adapters — pure assets with no behaviour of their own.
arch.note: The self-developed core is under active development — we publish what the gates prove, nothing more.
watch.title: Four marks on one continuous line.
watch.sub: Most assistants begin when you speak. AiDog begins by holding context — then noticing, weighing, preparing, and stopping where your authority starts.
watch.b1b: Heartbeats, memory, releases, cost — the signals that belong to your world, gathered without you asking.
watch.b2b: Most drift is noise. The rare ones arrive with a reason, a severity, and a sentence you can act on.
watch.b3b: A diff, a plan, a way back. Prepared in full, executed by no one until you say so.
watch.b4b: Constitution, memory and skills travel with you. No single machine gets to hold your dog hostage.
counsel.title: Quiet until it isn't.
counsel.sub: A notification tells you something changed. The counsel tells you why it matters, what it would do, and where your say begins.
counsel.note: Preview only · no live service · nothing sent
counsel.letterTitle: Sir, the picture has shifted slightly.
counsel.letterBody: Two deployment checks no longer match yesterday's baseline. The last release completed cleanly and no outage signal is present, so I have not treated this as urgent — but it will matter before your next deployment. I have prepared a review of the diff and a way back. Nothing has been sent, changed, or scheduled.
cert.title: What it may never do to you.
cert.sub: Power is only useful when you can see why it moved, stop it, and take it with you. These are not settings — they are the terms of the relationship.
cert.freeBody: No paid tier, no usage fee, no feature gate. One dog, one owner — not a platform that grows to need your money.
